beforeQuestion.prompt: In a podcast production desk, the episode producer must replace a source recording while preserving annotations. Annotations follow stable segments rather than file offsets. The interview lens is “Happy paths, alternate flows, errors, and exceptional scenarios”: apply it without relying on a pattern name. The design review now adds a second workflow variant. This is a new requirement: which decision best preserves the contract?

currentQuestion.prompt: An episode editor replaces a recording by stable segment IDs. Four annotations still match; one annotation points to a segment removed from the replacement. No annotation may silently disappear, and the producer can repair the unmatched one. The producer reviews only complete replacement revisions; no partial revision becomes active. Which result should the replacement operation return?

options.text: Reject the complete replacement and name the unmatched segment; keep the current recording active.
Apply four mappings and queue the unmatched annotation for manual follow-up, reporting the new recording active with a warning.
Activate the new recording and attach the unmatched annotation to the nearest timestamp, treating proximity as a substitute for segment identity.

feedback.reason: A rejected result preserves the all-or-nothing observable promise while naming the actionable conflict; the producer can correct the mapping and resubmit.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An alternate-path decision is complete only when the caller can distinguish what the command actually accepted from what it rejected or left unresolved. Here, the unmatched annotation must remain intact and can be repaired before retry.
details.scenarioApplication: An episode editor replaces a recording by stable segment IDs. Four annotations still match; one annotation points to a segment removed from the replacement. No annotation may silently disappear, and the producer can repair the unmatched one. In this case, returns a rejected replacement with the unmatched segment ID; the caller can follow the stated recovery or follow-up path.
details.errorCorrection: Partial application loses one annotation despite the explicit no-loss promise. Timestamp proximity is not a stated identity rule and can silently attach a note to the wrong segment.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the product later permits partial replacements, that must be an explicit result with each unmatched annotation retained for resolution, not an implicit success.
details.transfer: For a multi-part change, make the returned outcome distinguish complete acceptance from unresolved elements whenever callers must act on the remainder.

messages.text: Queueing the unmatched annotation preserves it but still exposes a partial revision as active, contrary to the complete-revision rule.
Timestamp proximity is not a stated identity rule and can silently attach a note to the wrong segment.

currentQuestion.prompt: A temporary review role is granted only after approval by two named reviewers. The second reviewer revoked consent before the grant command is processed. The request includes the approval record IDs. Which caller-visible outcome is appropriate?

currentQuestion.prompt: A notary submits an immutable document revision to an external signer. The signer may have accepted the request before the connection timed out, and the same request ID can be queried. The notary must not create a second seal. options.text: Return signing-failed and retry with a fresh request ID, treating the timeout as proof the signer never accepted the first request.
Return signed once the request reaches the signer endpoint, assuming delivery to the endpoint means the signer accepted it.

details.errorCorrection: The signer may have accepted, so failure is not established and a new ID risks duplication. Reaching an endpoint does not prove the signer accepted or completed the seal.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Only a signer response or query result can resolve the pending state; elapsed time alone does not turn an unknown outcome into success or failure.

currentQuestion.prompt: A meter reservation request overlaps an existing committed discharge window. Which outcome fits a collision?

currentQuestion.prompt: A receipt service depends on a tax provider, but outage behavior and legal fallback are unknown. What note prevents the design from promising an unsupported result?

options.text: Draw a provider call and assume it always responds.
Add an offline tax table without confirming its legal validity.
Mark provider/fallback assumptions, decision owner, and conditional flow.
Leave the provider off the view because its behavior is unknown.

feedback.reason: An unknown outage/fallback condition can change the receipt contract; an unconditional path overstates what is known.
